title: The Quiet Library Alarm
story:
The town library used a quiet alarm. It did not ring. It flashed a small red light at the desk when a book left without a proper loan. On Thursday the light flashed for a book that was still on the shelf. Librarian Greta checked the shelf twice. The book, a guide to local birds, was in the right place, but the light kept flashing.

A student named Paul had stood near that shelf all afternoon. He said he had read a few pages and put the book back. Greta believed him, yet the alarm stayed on. She looked more carefully. A second copy was missing from the row, and a thin metal strip from an old label was stuck inside Paul's notebook. That strip was the part that set the alarm off. It had fallen from a book he had returned the week before.

Paul had not taken anything. He emptied the notebook, and the light went dark. Greta fixed the strip back into the returned book and tested the gate. The alarm stayed quiet, which was normal when every loan was correct. She thanked Paul for waiting. Paul checked his bag again in case another strip was hiding. He said a quiet alarm can still cause a loud worry. Greta closed the notebook and smiled at him. Greta wrote a note to check loose strips at the end of each day.

quiz.question: How did the alarm warn the staff?
options: It flashed a small red light
It rang a loud bell
It locked the front door
It sent a letter home
quiz.correctAnswer: It flashed a small red light
quiz.explanation: The quiet alarm flashed a small red light at the desk.
quiz.supportingSentence: It flashed a small red light at the desk when a book left without a proper loan.

quiz.question: Which book was still on the shelf?
options: A guide to local birds
Paul's notebook
A book returned last week
A book with no label
quiz.explanation: The guide to local birds was still in the right place.
quiz.supportingSentence: The book, a guide to local birds, was in the right place, but the light kept flashing.

quiz.question: What was stuck inside the notebook?
options: A thin metal strip from an old label
The guide to local birds
A red light from the desk
Greta's closing note
quiz.correctAnswer: A thin metal strip from an old label
quiz.explanation: A thin metal strip from an old label was stuck in Paul's notebook.
quiz.supportingSentence: A second copy was missing from the row, and a thin metal strip from an old label was stuck inside Paul's notebook.

quiz.question: In this story, what is a loan?
options: Letting a reader borrow a book
A red light at the desk
A thin piece of metal
A note written at closing time
quiz.correctAnswer: Letting a reader borrow a book
quiz.explanation: A loan is when a reader borrows a book in the correct way.
quiz.supportingSentence: The alarm stayed quiet, which was normal when every loan was correct.

quiz.question: Was the alarm broken on Thursday?
options: No, it reacted to a loose strip
Yes, it only worked on Friday
Yes, Greta had turned it off
No, the building had no alarm
quiz.correctAnswer: No, it reacted to a loose strip
quiz.explanation: The strip set the alarm off, so the alarm was working.
quiz.supportingSentence: That strip was the part that set the alarm off.
